sections.title: Habitats
lines: Any jungle
Tropical and subtropical rain forests

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A twelve-foot beetle with a horn about six feet long and a frequently bright or iridescent shell.

sections.title: Attacks mechanics
lines: Mandibles and horn · The mandibles deal 3d6 damage, and the single horn deals 2d8 damage.

sections.title: Habitat and behavior mechanics
lines: Jungle forager · It looks for fruit and vegetation in the rain forest and may crush obstacles in its path.

sections.title: Table notes

Herbivore. Elite (14) morale.
Nonintelligent (0). Neutral. Treasure, special attacks, special defenses and magic resistance Nil. No fixed HP.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, third printing (January 1994), pp. 18–19.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Any forest
Cultivated fields adjoining woodland

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A ten-foot beetle with two long horns, usually each at least eight feet long.

sections.title: Attacks mechanics
lines: Paired horns · The table gives a first attack for 4–16 damage and one attack with each horn for 1–10. The text identifies the horns and leaves the first attack unnamed.

sections.title: Habitat and behavior mechanics
lines: Crop raids · It feeds chiefly on grain and other crops. A raid can strip a farm and stampede livestock. A hungry Stag Beetle may also eat livestock.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Fresh water at least 30 feet deep

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A six-foot air-breathing beetle that carries a bubble under its wings.

sections.title: Habitat and behavior mechanics
lines: Freshwater hunter · It hunts by scent and by feeling vibrations. Water beetles sometimes attack and sink vessels on rivers and lakes. The source gives no separate vessel attack or damage values.
Air bubble · It carries air under its wings to stay underwater for extended periods and can release a bubble into a cave or other cavity that will hold it. The description gives no duration.
